issues.description: README diff smuggles unrelated refactors and reformatting into a test-focused PR
issues.detail: The PR claims to add POST tests but the README diff also reorders StorageError.handle parameters, swaps str(status_code)+reason for code_to_http_status, and switches stream to bounded_stream throughout. These are three separate semantic changes hidden under a reformat. Split into separate PRs so reviewers can audit each change in scope.

issues.description: Switch from req.stream to req.bounded_stream is the load-bearing fix but undocumented and unjustified
issues.detail: things_advanced.py changes body = req.stream.read() to req.bounded_stream.read(). These have different contracts: bounded_stream enforces Content-Length, stream does not. This is the actual semantic change that makes the new 400 test pass, yet it gets one line, no comment, no versionchanged note. Document why bounded_stream is correct here.

issues.description: FAQ example is over-elaborate and obscures the lesson it claims to teach
issues.detail: The FAQ section is meant to show how to set headers in tests, but PostTest layers Content-Length checks, conditional reads, and three status codes with nested control flow. Strip to the smallest handler that demonstrates the point, flatten the branches into guarded returns, and state the precondition explicitly.

issues.description: FAQ example uses parenthesized assert, a known pytest footgun
issues.detail: assert(result.status == falcon.HTTP_400) reads like a function call and silently passes when given a tuple. FAQ code gets copied. Rewrite as assert result.status == falcon.HTTP_400.

issues.description: New POST tests assert status codes without naming the contract under test
issues.detail: resp3 and resp4 check status codes but no docstring or comment states which invariant of things_advanced is being verified (auth + JSON + body-required). Future maintainers reading a failure will not know whether the 400 is spec or accident. Add a one-line spec comment per assertion block, and consider factoring shared header dict.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the underlying change is small and reasonable — two POST regression tests plus a bounded_stream fix in the example — but the PR has a scope problem. The README diff smuggles three unrelated semantic changes (handle signature reorder, code_to_http_status swap, bounded_stream switch) under a reformatting commit and should be split. The load-bearing fix (req.stream to req.bounded_stream) is undocumented despite being the reason the new 400 test passes. The FAQ example is more elaborate than the lesson it teaches and contains a parenthesized-assert footgun. None of these block merge on correctness, but scope and spec discipline are thin.
